transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
President Trump signed an executive order last night, exempting Russia from sweeping
economic sanctions just passed by Congress and that were set to take place in days.
Ukraine's President Zelensky calls the move unfortunate and says Trump's recent announcement
that the U.S. would buy diesel from Russia won't make a lot of difference.
The volume is not enough, it's not enough for the United States, but it's quite enough
for Russia to spend more money, much money on the war.
I'm sure this diesel will not help Americans, but will help Putin.
I don't know all the reasons, and it's pity.
I think that we have to be true partners.
Zelensky speaking there to NPR's Joanna Kokissis in an interview in Kiev earlier this week.
This is Russia has stepped up airstrikes while Ukraine's military also saw disruptions to
intelligence sharing and access to starlink that left front lines and Ukrainian cities
vulnerable.
Lawyers for Congresswoman Ilion Omar are demanding the Justice Department return all properties
seized by federal agents in a search over Minnesota home this week.
And Piers Ryan Lucas has more.
In a letter to the Justice Department, Omar's attorneys call the investigation a vindictive,
retributive and politically motivated effort to go after one of President Trump's chief
critics in Congress.
They point out that the court-authorized search of Omar's home in Washington, D.C., took place
just weeks before the midterm elections, which violates a longstanding Justice Department
norm that aims to avoid taking action that could be perceived as interfering in an election.
Federal agents seized Omar's phone, computer and documents during their search of her home
as part of an investigation into possible immigration fraud.
Omar was born in Somalia and came to the U.S. as a child.
Her attorneys say there is no legitimate basis to suggest that Omar violated any law concerning
her citizenship status.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News.
Thousands of No Kings events are taking place around the country today.
And this year, they're focusing on voting and increasing voting participation.
Michael Brown from member station WGCU has more.
Keely Armstrong of Fort Myers says she's a Democrat, but she wants everyone to get more
involved in the political process.
I'm hoping to send the message that it's important to vote no matter what your political party
is, because if we don't get out and vote, we can't change what we don't like.
A short step away, a figure dressed as Lady Liberty held a sparkling flame and waved as
vehicles honked.
That is Diane Ciri.
The construction company owner and Democrat says she wants everyone to get out to vote.
To end this nonsense.
Ciri says she has one main reason for being there.
I'm hoping to see a lot of these corrupt politicians come to justice.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Brown in Fort Myers.
You're listening to NPR News in Washington.
The U.S. territory of Guam is bracing for a super typhoon.
Typhoon Champy, currently a Category 4 storm, is expected to pass just south of the island.
Dana Williams from member station KPRG on Guam has more.
Residents of Guam were urged to secure their homes and evacuate from low-lying coastal
areas as the dangerous typhoon approached the island.
Brandon Eitlett of the National Weather Service on Guam described the situation as a near-worst-case
scenario.
Champy is rapidly intensifying, and we are looking at a Category 4 150-mph super typhoon
at the time early Sunday morning around closest point of approach.
Residents were warned to take shelter in reinforced concrete buildings and to remain in place
until the all clear is given.
Forecasters said the island will likely experience widespread power outages, possibly lasting
for days or weeks.
Champy will be the third super typhoon to hit the Mariana Island chain in the western
Pacific this year.
For NPR News, I'm Dana Williams on Guam.
Pope Leo is out of the hospital days after having lung cancer surgery.
Yesterday, he celebrated mass in the hospital in Rome, and tomorrow he's scheduled to
deliver the traditional noon blessing from a window overlooking St. Peter's Square.
The 71-year-old had the lower lobe of his right lung removed and test results on whether
the cancer had spread.
Aren't in yet.
He's got a trip to Latin America scheduled for next month.
The Vatican, though, hasn't commented on whether that will still take place.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.

Zelensky tells NPR Trump's Russian diesel purchase announcement won't meaningfully help Ukraine
Russia steps up airstrikes as Ukraine faces disrupted US intelligence sharing and Starlink access
Lawyers for Rep. Ilhan Omar demand Justice Department return property seized in home search
No Kings protests across the country this weekend focus on increasing voter participation
Typhoon Champi, a Category 4 storm, threatens Guam with widespread power outages expected
Pope Leo leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery; cancer spread test results pending
Pope Leo to deliver noon blessing from window overlooking St. Peter's Square
